chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Jameel, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
I said to him, 'A man leaves his daughter, and his sister from his father and his mother.' So he said, 'The wealth, all of it, is for his daughter.'

key_terms.لِأَبِيهِ وَ أُمِّهِ: from his father and his mother (paternal and maternal sister)

ai.seo_question: Who inherits the entire estate when a man leaves behind both a daughter and a sister?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi clarifies the principle of 'blocking' (hijr) in Shia inheritance jurisprudence, where the presence of a closer heir (the daughter) excludes a more distant one (the sister). It highlights the specific scenario where the deceased leaves behind parents, yet the daughter still inherits the entire estate, demonstrating the precedence of direct descendants over ascendants and collaterals in this context. This ruling is foundational for understanding the distribution of the 'Fara'id' (fixed shares) versus 'Dhawi al-Arqab' (holders of the neck/primary heirs).

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Jameel, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>,
‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘A man leaves his daughter, and his sister from his father and his mother’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The wealth, all of it, is for his daughter’.
en.sarwar: 8. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Musa ibn Bakr from Ali ibn Sa‘id who has narrated the following:

“Zurarah once asked me, ‘What do you say about a man who leaves behind his parents and brothers from his mother?’ I replied, ‘The share of mother is one-sixth and the rest belongs to the father. ‘If there are brothers the share of the mother is one-sixth.’ He said, ‘These brothers are from the father. Brothers from father and mother receive the largest amount. Brothers from mother receive one-third and she receives one-sixth. It is one-sixth because brothers from father and brothers from father and mother bar her. The father spends on them so his share is expanded and the share of the mother is reduced for that reason. Brothers from the mother are not in it. They do not bar their mother from receiving one-third.’ I then asked, ‘Do brothers inherit from the mother anything?’ He said, ‘There is no doubt in it, it is just as I say to you.’”
